rendered: The paper does not report any leaching amount for nickel, manganese or cobalt. It states that their relative ratios in NMC622 stayed consistent before and after separation, so the process does not leach those metals.[1][2][3] The authors say ICP-OES confirmed this, but the numbers are only in the supplementary Table S1, which is not part of this document.[4] The only leaching the paper reports is of lithium, which it says occurred after recovery. It attributes this to the Cyrene molecule having two[5] ether groups that attract lithium cations because ether is electron-donating, resulting in lithium leaching and making the high-Ni cathode more unstable.[6][7] The paper also says the electrochemical degradation may be due to both lithium leaching and possible surface changes caused by the Cyrene solvent.[8]
